question.text: Section 90A of the Income Tax Act deals with:

answer.text: Unilateral relief for taxpayers from countries without a DTAA with India
Transfer pricing adjustments for cross-border transactions
Tax relief under DTAAs signed between the Government of India and foreign governments
Agreements between specified associations in India and foreign countries for double taxation relief

explanation.text: The Logic: The Income Tax Act allocates DTAA-style relief across three closely related sections. Section 90 covers agreements between the Government of India and the governments of foreign countries. Section 90A specifically empowers the Central Government to adopt agreements entered into between specified associations in India and specified associations in foreign countries for the purpose of granting double-taxation relief, exchange of information, and recovery assistance. Section 91 provides unilateral relief where no DTAA exists. So Section 90A is the "specified-associations" route — the answer matching that scope. The Trap: Unilateral relief for non-DTAA countries is Section 91, not Section 90A. Transfer-pricing adjustments live in Sections 92 to 92F. Government-to-government DTAAs are Section 90. Each option maps to a different section and only the specified-associations description fits Section 90A. Note: The cited NISM Series X-B Investment Adviser Level 2 workbook pages reviewed in the audit explain general DTAA residence/source taxation, DTAA rates, TRC/Form 10F, and dividend beneficial-owner rates, but do not mention Section 90A or agreements between specified associations on the pages checked. The framing above reflects general Indian Income Tax Act knowledge.
